title: Introduction to Simple Graphs on the Cartesian Plane

blocks.text: Imagine you are at Balogun market, and you want to find a friend's shop using a map. How would you use coordinates to locate it?

blocks.markdown: In mathematics, we often use a grid called the Cartesian plane to locate points and draw graphs. This grid helps us understand relationships between numbers visually.

blocks.title: Cartesian Plane
blocks.text: The Cartesian plane is a two-dimensional grid formed by two perpendicular lines called axes: the horizontal axis (x-axis) and the vertical axis (y-axis).

blocks.markdown: Each point on the plane is represented by a pair of numbers known as coordinates, written as \((x, y)\). The first number \(x\) tells us how far to move horizontally, and the second number \(y\) tells us how far to move vertically.

blocks.title: Plotting a Point
blocks.prompt: Plot the point \((3, 2)\) on the Cartesian plane.

steps.text: Move 3 units to the right along the x-axis.
Move 2 units up along the y-axis.

blocks.answer: The point \((3, 2)\) is located 3 units to the right and 2 units up from the origin.

blocks.markdown: Graphs of linear relationships are straight lines. To draw a simple linear graph, we use a table of values to find points that lie on the line.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: Always label your axes and mark your points clearly when drawing graphs. This helps avoid mistakes and makes your graph easy to read.

points: The Cartesian plane is used to plot points and draw graphs.
Coordinates \((x, y)\) help locate points on the plane.
Linear graphs are straight lines that can be drawn using a table of values.
